record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a capability outcome from abliteration using a difference-in-means direction and weight edits, but does not report a direct reproduction of the original intervention and refusal measures.
record.gate_note: The README says small models lose more general capability from abliteration than 8B+ models. It gives no refusal rates or quantitative capability results. The statement that optimize did not improve on select is a comparison between the repo's methods and is not recorded as a result row.
record.test_reason: This is a tool repository. It applies the difference-in-means direction and abliteration (Arditi et al.) as a method and reports no refusal rates, capability numbers or evaluation outputs. Its only result is a one-line qualitative remark about its own tool's capability cost (README Limitations), with no baseline or magnitude. That is the method's own performance, not a test of whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents a toolkit that finds the Arditi-style refusal direction and removes it by weight edit or adapter on Qwen3 models. It warns, without numbers, that ≤4B models lose more general capability than 8B+. It also says the Heretic-style optimize search did not beat simple selection on Qwen3-8B. No quantitative results are reported.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. It measures harmful-versus-harmless activation differences by layer and template position, selects candidate directions by ablation, and edits weights or uses an adapter; the README does not report a complete original-method reproduction or its results.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says capability loss is greater for models ≤4B than for 8B+ models.
record.problems: The capability comparison is qualitative and not model-specific; no refusal rates, uncertainty estimates, or evaluation counts are reported in the README.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows are reported in the README. In particular, it gives no refusal-rate outcomes for the evaluation pipeline; the select-versus-optimize comparison is a comparison of the repo's own methods.

untested.parts: Whether ablation removes refusal (no rates reported), whether adding the direction induces refusal, and capability preservation in quantified form.
Refusal removal in released Qwen3 models (no eval results reported) and the quantified capability cost.

record.verdict_notes: I reclassified this from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4 and dropped the reader's limits_scope labels, since no refusal or capability numbers are reported. Other README remarks are qualitative usage notes about the tool, not measured results: abliterating a fine-tuned model 'can erase what it learned', and domain fine-tuning 'can bring [refusals] back'.

versions.untested_parts: No reported refusal rates; no test of adding the direction; no test of ablating it from every layer and position. The capability result is not quantified.
No reported refusal rates or quantitative evidence that weight edits remove refusal in released models. The capability result is not quantified.

rows.subject: Qwen3 family (models ≤4B; aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Abliteration using candidate refusal directions; the README does not specify which model or edit produced this comparison.
rows.value: Small models lose more general capability from abliteration than 8B+ models.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison only; no model-specific results or magnitude of capability loss are given.
rows.check: This is an unquantified Limitations bullet: no baseline, no perplexity values, no refusal rates, and no named model or edit. The state 'partial' cannot be read from it. It describes the tool's own performance, so it is better treated as context than as a test result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
